warmup.description: Gently awaken the spine, breath, and deep core stabilizers with slow, mindful movement.

main_exercises.name: Spinal Articulation Flow
main_exercises.load_guidance: Bodyweight only, focus on segmented movement through the spine
main_exercises.form_cue: Move one vertebra at a time, starting from the tailbone upward

main_exercises.name: Supine Core Stability Sequence
main_exercises.load_guidance: Bodyweight only, maintain deep abdominal engagement throughout
main_exercises.form_cue: Keep lower back gently connected to the mat without gripping

main_exercises.name: Side-Lying Leg Control Series
main_exercises.form_cue: Move from the hip joint without shifting torso alignment

main_exercises.name: Quadruped Stability Flow
main_exercises.load_guidance: Bodyweight only, emphasize balance over range
main_exercises.form_cue: Keep hips level and avoid collapsing into the supporting shoulder

main_exercises.name: Standing Postural Alignment Sequence
main_exercises.form_cue: Stack ribs over pelvis and lengthen through crown of head

cooldown.description: Downregulate the nervous system and release residual tension through breath-led stretching.
movements: Child’s pose with deep breathing x 60s

phase_notes.menstrual: This session supports recovery and can help reduce discomfort—move slowly and prioritize breath over range of motion. Keep everything gentle and restorative.
phase_notes.follicular: Use this session to reinforce alignment and body awareness—small increases in control and precision can enhance strength work later in the cycle.
phase_notes.ovulatory: Even in higher-energy phases, keep this session soft and grounding—focus on control rather than pushing range or intensity.
phase_notes.early_luteal: This is an ideal phase for this type of Pilates work—use it to maintain stability and manage early signs of fatigue or tension.
phase_notes.late_luteal: Highly supportive for this phase—focus on breath-led movement and nervous system downregulation to reduce stress and physical discomfort.
